quizzes.stem: A sales team's Project holds a price list saved as a file in March. Finance revises that list every month in a cloud-hosted document, and reps keep quoting March figures. What is the best fix?

options.a: Add each month's file next to the old ones and keep every one of them in view
options.b: Tell the instructions to favour whichever figure looks most recent in the files
options.c: Ask Claude to mention any figure it feels unsure about at the end of each reply
options.d: Replace the snapshot with a synced Drive link, so the newest edition is read

explanation.d: A synced document follows its source, so the next read gets the latest version (connecting a document instead of copying it).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "an instruction is a request and a deleted file is a guarantee", and the old figure would still be in the knowledge base.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Quality in is quality out", and asking for self-doubt does not repair a stale source.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Two versions of one document side by side invite Claude to quote either".

quizzes.stem: In March a colleague pastes the refund percentage into a Project's instructions. In June the policy changes, the team deletes the March policy file and uploads the June one, yet July replies still quote the March percentage. What explains it?

options.a: A second copy of the figure sits in text that no replaced document reaches
options.b: Memory carried the March percentage over from an earlier conversation
options.c: The old and new editions both remain in the knowledge base, and Claude quotes either
options.d: Sharing the Project keeps showing members the percentage they saw first

explanation.a:
Instructions say how to work and files say what is true, so a figure typed into the instructions is a
   second copy that no file update will touch (the first trap).
explanation.b:
Ruled out because memory "holds preferences
   and context that Claude picked up, not the authoritative text of a policy".
explanation.c:
Ruled out because the team
   deleted the March file, whereas the page warns about "Two versions of one document side by side".
explanation.d:
is ruled
   out because "anyone with access can read the instructions and every file in the knowledge base" describes who
   sees the content, not whether it is current.

quizzes.stem: An operations lead supports several clients, whose background material and house rules must never mix. Which set-up fits?

options.a: Run one long chat and paste each customer's material into it in turn as the work arrives
options.b: Create one Project and put all customers' guidance into a single instruction block
options.c: Give each customer a Project holding that customer's own instructions and documents
options.d: Depend on memory alone, since Claude saves context from every chat it has

explanation.c: Each Project is a self-contained space, so "one Project's context does not leak into another" (the memory paragraph).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Everything in a Project competes for the context window", and one block of mixed rules lets one customer's rules bleed into another's.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the table says chats are "The actual tasks; each can be restarted without losing the first two", and one long chat gives that up.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "memory is not a substitute for a knowledge file" and holds preferences, not each customer's authoritative documents.

quizzes.stem: A consultant must hand a client a one-page dashboard that the client will open, adjust and forward. The consultant also wants to try a different layout without losing the first one. Which approach fits?

options.a: An inline reply, with each layout pasted into a fresh chat and compared by eye
options.b: An artifact, with the alternative started by editing an earlier message
options.c: A skill, with each layout saved as its own custom skill in the account
options.d: A Research run, with each layout requested as a new report with citations

explanation.b:
An artifact opens in its own panel for editing and sharing, and editing an earlier message branches the
   chat so "each branch has its own artifact".
explanation.a:
Ruled out because an artifact opens in a panel "so you can
   edit and re-use it without scrolling back through a conversation".
explanation.c:
Ruled out because a skill is "A
   repeatable procedure used across many chats", not a deliverable the client can open.
explanation.d:
is ruled out because
   Research is for "An open question that needs many sources and citations", and this task has known content to lay
   out.

quizzes.stem: A finance team builds its monthly report inside a Project called Finance. A manager who works in separate chats outside that Project needs the same house layout. Which feature carries that procedure to both places?

options.a: Written rules in the Finance Project's own instructions
options.b: A plugin installed for the whole department
options.c: An artifact kept as the pattern for each new report
options.d: A custom skill that Claude loads when the task matches

explanation.d:
A skill is a reusable procedure that Claude pulls in "in any chat where it is enabled", inside or outside
   a Project.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because "Project instructions apply to every chat in that Project", and the manager's
   chats sit elsewhere.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because a plugin is "A role's bundle of procedures and connections", far
   more than one layout.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because an artifact is "A document, deck, dashboard or small tool to hand
   to someone" and does not make later chats follow a layout.

quizzes.stem: A colleague shares a ZIP file of a "free time-saving skill" from an unknown site and asks you to upload it. What is the best response?

options.a: Upload it straight away, since skills only run when the task matches them
options.b: Inspect the archive first, and decline unless someone trusted vouches for it
options.c: Upload it for yourself only, so that no colleague is ever exposed to it
options.d: Upload it to a test chat and judge it by the first reply it gives back to you

explanation.b: Skills carry instructions and scripts that Claude follows, so the page says to install skills only from trusted sources and to review what they bundle.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "from an unknown source it is a route for prompt injection", whether or not the task matches.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the risks named, "prompt injection and data exfiltration", apply to the person who installs the skill, not only to colleagues.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the first reply cannot show hidden scripts or instructions, which is why the page says to review "code dependencies and bundled resources" first.

quizzes.stem: A manager links the company's cloud storage, then asks Claude to summarise a restricted finance directory. Claude cannot find it, although an administrator colleague sees it in the same storage. What explains this?

options.a: The tool carries the signed-in person's rights, which exclude that location
options.b: The tool reads only material above a certain age, and that area is newer
options.c: The workspace holding the chat must be shared before the area becomes visible
options.d: The area is too big for retrieval to cope with in a single request

explanation.a: "Claude inherits each person's permissions from the connected service", so the manager's reach, not the administrator's, decides what appears.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page names permissions as the cause of a missing result ("the connector cannot reach it from Claude for them either") and says nothing about the age of material.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Fixing a connector's reach is done in the source system", not by sharing a workspace.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page ties a missing result to access, as in "the connector cannot reach it from Claude for them either", and never to size.

quizzes.stem: A company connects its helpdesk to Claude. Agents may read tickets and add internal notes freely, but ending a ticket must wait for a person's click, and trainees must not see escalated tickets. Which design meets both rules?

options.a: Require approval to close, and leave the group's limit in the source system itself
options.b: Allow every tool without approval and expect the helpdesk to stop the trainees
options.c: Require approval to close, and write the group's limit into the connector's instructions
options.d: Require approval to close, and give that group wider access through Claude's settings

explanation.a: Each tool can be set to need approval, and Claude inherits each person's permissions, so a restriction on one group belongs in the source system.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "Fixing a connector's reach is done in the source system,
   by changing who can open what, not by rewording an instruction".
explanation.b:
Ruled out because an organisation can
   "let Claude read a system and require a human click before it writes to it", and always allowing every tool gives
   that up.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A connector cannot give anyone more access than they already have".

quizzes.stem: A team lead finds a handy link on a forum that would add a custom connector in seconds. What is the best step?

options.a: Install it, then watch the first few replies for anything odd
options.b: Install it on the free plan first, since that permits one trial server
options.c: Check who operates it, and which scopes it requests, before approving
options.d: Install it in On demand mode, which restricts what the server can do

explanation.c: The checklist says to connect only to servers from trusted organisations and to read the scopes before approving them.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a custom connector has not been verified by Anthropic", whatever the plan allows.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Remote tools can change after you approve them", so a good first reply proves nothing about later behaviour.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the page suggests On demand when you have ten or more connectors", which is about tool loading and not about what a server may do.

quizzes.stem: A recruiter's Project answers hiring questions from a policy file that HR revises each quarter in a shared drive. The recruiter wants current answers without re-uploading, and wants candidate notes unseen by others who have access. Which design fits?

options.a: Upload the latest version each period, and share the space so HR can check it
options.b: Sync the source document, and leave private material out of the knowledge
options.c: Type the policy wording into the instructions, since those are always read
options.d: Switch on Research for every question, so the wording is looked up on the web

explanation.b: A synced document follows its source, and the knowledge base is readable by everyone with access, so private notes stay out (pages 1 and 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "an uploaded file is a copy as of the day you uploaded it", and sharing exposes everything the knowledge holds.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A figure typed into the instructions is a second copy that no file update will touch".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Do not use it for a question that one document answers", and a policy file is that case.

quizzes.stem: A department wants a monthly report in one layout, built from figures kept in a shared spreadsheet and delivered to a client in editable form. Which combination fits best?

options.a: A Project for the data, a plugin for the buyer and a skill for the output
options.b: Research for the data, memory for the procedure and an inline reply for the output
options.c: A skill for the procedure, a connector for the data, an artifact for the output
options.d: Three separate chats, one per stage, with material copied across by hand

explanation.c: A skill carries a repeatable procedure, a connector reads live data, and an artifact is a deliverable someone can open and edit.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A short answer stays inline in the chat", which does not suit a file to be edited.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a plugin is "A role's bundle of procedures and connections", and not the means of handing one deliverable to one buyer.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A skill is a reusable procedure Claude pulls in when the task matches", which copying by hand gives up.

quizzes.stem: A new hire installs a free skill found on a public forum. Its page says the skill also needs a custom connector to the hire's work email, and the hire's plan allows both. Which step belongs before installing?

options.a: Confirm that the plan lists skills and custom connectors, then install it
options.b: Trial it in a private chat first and judge it by the first few replies
options.c: Install it on the hire's account only, so colleagues stay out of reach
options.d: Inspect the package contents and confirm who operates the server it calls

explanation.d:
A skill carries instructions and scripts that Claude follows, and a custom connector "has not been
   verified by Anthropic", so the contents and the operator need checking first.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because "A skill
   can carry scripts and instructions that Claude follows", so plan availability says nothing about safety.
explanation.b:
is
   ruled out because the page says to "review code dependencies and bundled resources first", and a first reply
   cannot show them.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "The page names prompt injection and data exfiltration as the most
   significant risks", and the mailbox in danger is the installer's own.

quizzes.stem: Two colleagues ask the same shared Project about one finance folder. One receives a summary, the other is told nothing was found. Both reached the storage through the same custom connector, which the owner enabled. What should the owner check first?

options.a: Reconnect the storage for the second colleague under the owner's credentials
options.b: Compare what each of them is allowed to see in the source system
options.c: Switch the connector to On demand so tools stop crowding the chat
options.d: Reword the Project instructions to search the whole folder

explanation.b:
Claude inherits each person's permissions, so two people can get different answers because they can see
   different files.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a connector "does not bypass the source system's permissions".
explanation.d:
is
   ruled out because "Fixing a connector's reach is done in the source system, by changing who can open what, not by
   rewording an instruction".
explanation.c:
Ruled out because On demand is suggested "when you have ten or more connectors,
   so that the conversation is not crowded with tools", which is about loading and not about reach.
